standard.title: Sports Footwear — Part 1: General Purpose (First Revision)
standard.description: This standard prescribes requirements, methods of sampling, and test procedures for general-purpose sports footwear (such as walking, fitness, exercising, and light sports activities). It applies to footwear designed to minimize wear fatigue and maximize durability across varied general athletic environments, excluding high-performance specialized athletic footwear.

amendments.summary: Inserts Clause 3.4 defining 'Insock' as a removable or non-removable footwear component covering all or part of the insole. Substitutes Clause 4.2 to classify general-purpose sports footwear into two main usage categories: For Kids (standard English sizes per IS 1638) and For Adults (all other sizes per IS 1638, further divided into Type 1 and Type 2). Completely replaces Table 1 with updated whole footwear physical requirements.

Amends Table 1, Sl No. (x), col (3), col (4), col (5) to substitute 'Category 1 and Category 2' for 'Category I and Category II'. Substitutes Clause C-3.1 to specify the load cell capacity of the tensile testing machine (<= 50 kg with jaw separation speed of 100 ± 10 mm/min and least count of 0.01 kg). Corrects a typographical error in Clause C-6, substituting 'interface' for 'infaiterface'. Completely replaces G-1.6 and G-2.1.4 equations to standardize the percentage of compression set calculations.

qco.name: Footwear made from Leather and other Materials (Quality Control) Order

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Footwear made from Leather and other Materials (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, all general-purpose sports footwear manufactured, imported, distributed, or sold in India must carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Micro and small units (MSEs) are granted specific delayed implementation schedules, and export-only shipments are exempt. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to sports shoes.
requirements: Every sports shoe must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) on a secure label or embossed permanently, accompanied by the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L).

Footwear size categories are split into two groups based on age: a) Kids: Standard English sizes for children per IS 1638; b) Adults: Standard English sizes above kids' ranges, further divided into Type 1 and Type 2.
The insock, if used, cannot be removed without damaging the footwear. This is a mandatory safety requirement for Kids, Adults (Type 1), and Adults (Type 2).
To maintain ergonomic gait mechanics during fitness and walking, the minimum toe spring height must be 2 mm for all categories (Kids, Adults Type 1, and Adults Type 2).
The heel/seat region must demonstrate high impact cushioning. The test is performed using a standard compression punch per IS 15298 (Part 1) to apply forces up to 6 000 N.

Outsoles must resist wear: a) Outsole abrasion is tested separately for cellular and solid outsoles; b) PU outsoles must pass a hydrolysis test to ensure they do not crumble in wet climates; c) Complete shoe flexing is evaluated per IS 8085 (Part 16) / ISO 24266 Method A.
Tensile testing machines used for checking bond strength must use a load cell with a capacity of <= 50 kg, jaw separation speed of 100 ± 10 mm/min, and a high-precision least count of 0.01 kg.

The exact mathematical compression set percentage must be calculated and expressed using the formula: 
Percent compression set = (t0 - ti) x 100 / t0, where t0 is initial thickness and ti is final thickness after recovery.
